### loading libraries
```{r message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)

```

# Problem 2

## loading and cleaning the demographics data

```{r message = FALSE}
demo_df = read_csv("nhanes_covar.csv",
                   na = c("", ".", "NA"),
                   skip = 4) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  filter(age >= 21) |> 
  mutate(
    education = recode_values(education, 1 ~ "less than high school",
                              2 ~ "high school equivalent", 3 ~ "more than high school"),
    education = factor(education, 
                       levels = c("less than high school",
                                  "high school equivalent",
                                  "more than high school")),
    sex = recode_values(sex, 1 ~ "male", 2 ~ "female"),
    sex = as.factor(sex)
  )

```

## loading and cleaning the accelerometer data
```{r message = FALSE}

accel_df = read_csv("nhanes_accel.csv",
                    na = c("", ".", "NA")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute",
    names_prefix = "min",
    values_to = "mims_value"
  ) |> 
  mutate(minute = as.numeric(minute))

```

## merging datasets

```{r}
combined_accel = left_join(demo_df, accel_df, by = "seqn")
```

## data visualizations of gender and education

```{r}

# table

demo_df |> 
  count(education,sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()

# visualization

demo_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x= sex, y = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Age distribution by sex and education",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```


From the table, it appears the number of males and females is relatively
equal among those with less than a high school education and more than a high 
school education, and there are more males than females with a high school 
equivalent education. 

To visualize the data, I chose a box plot because after trying a box plot, 
histogram, and density plot, I thought it was the clearest way to see
the spread of the data. Males and females with more than a high school education
have the youngest median age, while those with a high school equivalent education
are the oldest among females and those with less than a high school education
are the oldest among males. The spread of the data is similar among those with
more than or an equivalent high school education, while the age distribution
is a bit more condensed among those with less than a high school education. 
Within the high school equivalent education group the women have a notably higher
median age than men, while in the other education groups men and women have a 
similar median age.

## aggregated minutes

```{r}
combined_accel |> 
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) |> 
  summarize(total_mims = sum(mims_value)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total_mims, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total daily activity by age, sex, and education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total Activity by Monitor Indepedent Movement Summary (MIMS)"
  )
  
  
```

Across all three education levels, total activity decreases as age increases.
There is a steeper decrease among those with less than a high school education,
while the other two education groups have flatter slopes. Among those with less
than a high school education there is a slight increase in activity around those 
aged 60, among those with a high school equivalent there is an increase in 
activity from those aged 20 to those aged 40 (most notable among women), and 
then activity decreases, and among those with more than a high school education 
total activity generally decreases from 20 to 80, with a small bump among men 
aged 50 and women aged 60. Generally among education groups, men and women 
follow a similar pattern, but among those with less than a high school education 
the men typically have higher total activity (after age 40), while women have 
higher total activity among the other two education groups.
